lines: In an orchestra, there are many musicians.
There is someone who leads them, too.
The musicians learn if the music is fast, slow, quiet, or loud.
Conductors stand in front of the orchestra.
They hold a baton in their right hand.
Then, the musicians get ready to play.
The musicians look at the conductor's hands.
When the conductors move them slowly, the musicians play slowly.
When they move them quickly, the musicians play faster.
Conductors lead orchestras and make beautiful music.
body.text: In an orchestra, there are many musicians. There is someone who leads them, too. Guess who? A conductor! Conductors study the sheet music. They also teach the musicians. The musicians learn if the music is fast, slow, quiet, or loud. Conductors stand in front of the orchestra. They hold a baton in their right hand. They raise their hands. Then, the musicians get ready to play. Conductors move their hands. Then, the music starts. The musicians look at the conductor's hands. When the conductors move them slowly, the musicians play slowly. When they move them quickly, the musicians play faster. Conductors lead orchestras and make beautiful music.
